scope: Sparse figure digitization for comparison, not model-generated reference data
method: Manually selected isolated curve crossings; median of the nearest contiguous dark-pixel run (gray<100) on a 3-pixel slice within a 31-pixel search window. Coordinates refer to the declared private-source crops. No original raster is redistributed.
reading_uncertainty: Plus/minus3 pixels per coordinate is a practical reading envelope including line width and slight skew, not a statistical confidence interval. Calibration residual is reported separately. Independent reading and digitization have not yet been performed.
depletion_scope: FGH plots a/b only on the cold side and assumes a transition to normal abundances near n~1 cm^-3. Compare only the displayed portions; do not infer missing warm depleted curves.

printed_anchor.role: Rounded values in the text, not digitized points or fitted targets.

comparison_notes: Figure1 is scored as density at the digitized temperature, avoiding arbitrary branch selection near a vertical T(n) curve. Figure2 is scored at digitized density only when the model has a unique temperature root; otherwise all candidates are recorded and the point is unscored.

Pixel reading envelopes include3px and maximum axis-fit residual in each log coordinate. They do not describe model uncertainty, independent rereading, correlated calibration error, or the paper authors numerical precision.
No coefficients are fitted to the digitized points or the printed1800Kcm^-3 anchor. The baseline model is unchanged.

Sensitivity probes alter one implemented term at a time. They are diagnostics, not recovered atomic fits, probability bounds, or interchangeable physical models. In particular thermal Lyman-alpha multipliers leave the20eV superthermal collision point unchanged.
The original depleted curves are cold-side segments with an assumed transition to normal abundances near n~1cm^-3. No depleted warm branch is inferred from the source.
Figure2 electron ordinates are log10(1000*ne), not log10(ne); this factor is removed during calibration.
Source point statistics are descriptive sparse-reading discrepancies, not full-curve convergence or a historical validation pass.
